story.title: Introducing the Ford Privacy Promise: You're in Control of Your Data - Ford From the Road

facts.text: Ford has introduced a new Privacy Promise, publicly committing to protect customer vehicle data and give owners greater control over the information they share.

Jones reiterated that Ford's objective is to offer products and services that provide value to customers, not to monetize their personal information..Privacy Resources to Expand Beyond US.Ford said the Privacy Promise website will provide information about its privacy practices and available controls.

The company also plans to introduce privacy resources for Lincoln customers and users in Mexico and Canada in the coming weeks, with additional markets to follow.The initiative comes as connected vehicle technology becomes more widespread, making transparency around data collection and customer consent increasingly important..Join our WhatsApp Channel to get the latest news, exclusives and videos on WhatsApp
Ford Motor Co. in Dearborn is launching the Ford Privacy Promise to make an “explicit commitment to customers that their vehicle data is safe” and they’re in control of what they share.
As Ford created the Privacy Promise, it surveyed more than 1,000 U.S. consumers — both Ford and non-Ford owners.
It learned that while privacy is important to them, customers understand the value of data sharing.

“Even for a tech-savvy consumer, it can be hard to understand the relationship between your vehicle, the data it generates, and your privacy and rights,” says Kristin Jones, chief privacy officer and deputy general counsel for data and privacy at Ford.
“With our connected vehicle and app user communities growing every day, Ford takes its responsibility in safeguarding customer data seriously.”
Ford says it designs and builds its products with privacy in mind — from collection of data to its use, storage, and disposal.
This can include privacy-enhancing technologies like anonymizing or aggregating data to further protect a customer’s privacy.
As a result, Ford offers vehicle privacy settings that allow customers to control what data they want to share, subject to the features and services they wish to enjoy.
Ford stresses that it never sells data about how customers drive their vehicle to data brokers.
Data privacy has become an uncomfortable subject for America’s automakers.
Within days of General Motors agreeing to a $220 million settlement over how it handled driver information, Ford announced a new customer-facing commitment on the same issue.
GM must now restrict the driving data it collects and obtain a driver’s explicit consent before gathering or sharing it.
According to a report by MotorBiscuit , an outside party will also audit its privacy programs.
Earlier, in January 2025, it agreed with the Federal Trade Commission to stop sharing geolocation and driving-behavior data with consumer reporting agencies for five years.
It is not yet clear whether affected owners will receive any of the $220 million.
Against that backdrop, Ford has introduced the Ford Privacy Promise, which is meant to assure owners that their information is protected and that they decide what to share.
The data came from Smart Driver, a program that enrolled millions of motorists from 2016 until GM discontinued it in 2024.
To support the effort, Ford surveyed more than 1,000 U.S. customers about their understanding of data privacy.
Respondents overwhelmingly said they want the ability to control and adjust their privacy settings whenever they choose.
Ford says it develops its products with privacy in mind and tries to make clear how personal details are used.
MotorBiscuit is a digital-first platform covering the pulse of the automotive industry, motorsports, and more, part of the CG Digital Network.
Ford is launching the Privacy Promise to make an explicit commitment to customers that their vehicle data is safe with us and they’re in control of what they share.
Kristin Jones is Ford's Chief Privacy Officer and Deputy General Counsel, Data & Privacy.
